LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codebookOutputLaw: Draw M length-n codewords independently from a law q on words over a finite input alphabet. For a fixed message m, send its codeword through the block channel K, whose output alphabet may be arbitrary. The codebook–output law is the joint distribution of the entire sampled codebook and the resulting output word.

Draw the codewords independently from q on words over a finite input alphabet and send codeword m through a block channel K with arbitrary output alphabet. The sent codeword and the output then have joint distribution q(x)K(y|x).

Draw the M codewords independently from the same block law q on a finite input alphabet. Fix the sent index m and draw the output through the block channel K given codeword m. For any j ≠ m, codeword j and the output are independent. Their joint law is the product of q and the output law induced by q and K.
Given a codebook b with M ≥ 1 entries and an acceptance set A of word pairs, encode m as b(m). The decoder returns the least index j for which (b(j),y) lies in A, or index zero if no such j exists.
If (b(m),y) belongs to A and (b(j),y) lies outside A for every j ≠ m, decoding y using codebook b and acceptance set A returns m.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mean_codebookOutp: Let W be a memoryless channel with finite input and output alphabets. Draw M ≥ 1 codewords independently from q, transmit through Wⁿ and decode using the acceptance set A. Averaging the random-codebook error probability over uniformly chosen messages gives the same value as averaging each realized code’s uniform-message error over the distribution of codebooks.
